datasets.description: Source-reviewed signal evidence. Scope, period and status apply to each value; estimates and forecasts retain their qualifications.

rows.label: Egypt - 2024

rows.note: Figure given by the Minister of Communications and Information Technology at a meeting with the Egyptian Businessmen's Association, reported by TechAfrica News. Local mobile-phone production, not shipments, sales, exports or installed base. No definition or scope of 'production' is published.

rows.label: Egypt - 2025
rows.source: TechAfrica News / Egyptian Ministry of Communications and Information Technology
rows.note: Ministerial figure described as 'around 10 million' devices in 2025. Same definition and limits as the 2024 row. The statement's 2026 expectation of 14 to 15 million devices and its domestic demand estimate of 18 to 20 million are not recorded as observations: a forward figure does not enter a measured series.

datasets.title: Specialists exporting digital services
datasets.description: Source-reviewed signal evidence. Scope, period and status apply to each value; estimates and forecasts retain their qualifications.

rows.label: Egypt
rows.period: no reference year stated; as reported 2026-09-28
rows.source: Outsource Accelerator / Daily News Egypt
rows.note: Ministerial figure given at DevOpsDays Cairo 2026 and reported by Outsource Accelerator from Daily News Egypt. A workforce count for digital services exports, not employment in AI, not a hiring or wage measure and not an observed labour-market outcome. No definition of 'specialist', no reference year and no independent verification: not a national all-economy employment estimate.

datasets.title: Egyptian digital services export targets
datasets.description: Source-reviewed signal evidence. Scope, period and status apply to each value; estimates and forecasts retain their qualifications.

rows.label: Egypt - interim 2028 milestone

datasets.title: Teachers trained under Kenya's Digital Literacy Programme

rows.label: Kenya

datasets.description: Gross domestic product is the total income earned through the production of goods and services in an economic territory during an accounting period. It can be measured in three different ways: using either the expenditure approach, the income approach, or the production approach. The core indicator has been divided by the general population to achieve a per capita estimate.This indicator is expressed in current prices, meaning no adjustment has been made to account for price changes over time. This indicator is expressed in United States dollars. One current WDI vintage across all years. Historical values may be revised. Do not splice with older vintages; see the source definition for method changes.

datasets.title: Consumer price inflation — latest available
datasets.description: Inflation as measured by the consumer price index reflects the annual percentage change in the cost to the average consumer of acquiring a basket of goods and services that may be fixed or changed at specified intervals, such as yearly. datasets.title: Manufacturing value added — latest available
datasets.description: Manufacturing includes industries classified in ISIC (Rev. 3) major division C and is defined as the physical or chemical transformation of materials or components into new products. Value added is the contribution to the economy by a producer or an industry or an institutional sector, which is estimated by the total value of output produced and deducting the total value of intermediate consumption of goods and services used to produce that output. This indicator is expressed as a percentage of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) which is the total income earned through the production of goods and services in an economic territory during an accounting period. One current WDI vintage across all years. Historical values may be revised. Do not splice with older vintages; see the source definition for method changes.

datasets.title: Labour productivity — latest available
datasets.unit: GDP per person employed, constant 2021 PPP $
datasets.description: GDP per person employed is gross domestic product (GDP) divided by total employment in the economy. Purchasing power parity (PPP) GDP is GDP converted to 2021 constant international dollars using PPP rates. An international dollar has the same purchasing power over GDP that a U.S. dollar has in the United States. One current WDI vintage across all years. Historical values may be revised. Do not splice with older vintages; see the source definition for method changes.

rows.label: Algeria

Capacity is potential power, not annual generation or electricity consumed. No inference of dependable capacity or power available to data centres. One EIA data vintage. Historical estimates may be revised; source flags retained. National boundaries and coverage may change. No interpolation.

datasets.title: Eskom Homelight 20A electricity rate — latest available

Not a national average, municipal resale, industrial tariff or modelled household bill. Applicable tariff years start on 1 April. Flat-rate structure introduced in April 2025. Earlier inclining-block prices are incompatible and not joined. No foreign-exchange conversion. Rate validity ends 31 March of the next year; subsequent tariff changes need a new source review.
